ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Preventive Visit — Arthur Ashe — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Periodic adult preventive visit; no new concerns. [S]

Mr. Ashe is a 46-year-old man with HIV, diagnosed eleven months ago with cerebral toxoplasmosis and now well controlled on bictegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide, and with coronary artery disease after two bypass operations, who comes for his yearly preventive visit five weeks after his six-month review. His viral load was not detected at three and six months, and his CD4 count was 262 last month. He takes every dose and knows to keep any antacid, calcium, or iron well apart from his HIV tablet; he has needed none. He has had no chest pain and has not needed nitroglycerin. He hits tennis balls three times a week and is back to full-time writing and coaching. His right hand has stayed strong. His weight has come back to where it was before his illness. Mood is good. He has told one more close friend about his diagnosis, on his own terms, and says that went well. He has no new concerns. [S]

Follow-up: Nine-month HIV review in two months, with the influenza and COVID-19 vaccines and his decision about anal cancer screening. Colonoscopy through gastroenterology. Syphilis result by secure message. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 1989-10-19: nine-month HIV review: decision to stop toxoplasmosis maintenance therapy. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent, and a health care proxy form was completed; the agent is recorded in the confidential part of the chart and is not named here. He said that what matters most to him is staying active, his family, his work with young people, and keeping control of his own medical information. He chose not to record specific treatment preferences today. The plan will be revisited yearly or after any serious illness. [S]
